orders.text:
MCC No. 596/12 (Recall Application)
IN
AO No. 294/2012
Hon’ble V.K. Bist, J.
 Mr. Vinay Kumar, Standing Counsel for 
the applicant/State. 
 Mr. Hari Mohan Bhatia, Advocate for 
respondents. 
 Heard learned counsel for the parties. 
 On 17.07.2012, 48 hours time was granted 
to the counsel for the State to remove the 
defects pointed out by the Registry. It was also 
observed in the order that in case, defects are 
not removed within the stipulated time, the 
appeal shall stand dismissed without reference 
to the Bench. In compliance of that order, the 
defects were not removed within the stipulated 
time and the appeal stood dismissed without 
reference of the Bench. 
 Now instant application has been moved 
on behalf of the applicant/State seeking recall 
of the order dated 17.07.2012 on the ground 
that the matter relates to Uttarkashi and decree 
was to be obtained from District Court, 
Dehradun due to which efforts could not be 
made in order to remove the defects. 
 I have perused the order sheet. The 
appeal was filed on 28th June, 2012, thereafter 
time upto 5th July, 2012 was given for removing 
the defects and time was again extended upto 
10.07.2012. When the matter came on board on 
17.01.2012 again time was granted for removing 
the defects. It appears that the applicant/ 
appellant is not, at all, serious in the matter. In 
these circumstance, I was inclined to dismiss 
the recall application, but considering the 
veracity of the matter and in the interest of 
justice, I allow the recall application subject to 
payment of the cost of ` 2,000/-(Rs. Two 
thousand) to be paid to the High Court Legal  Services Committee within a period of one week 
from today. Counsel for the applicant/appellant 
shall produce a copy of receipt in the Registry 
within ten days from today. 
 In case, cost so imposed, is not paid, this 
order shall stand recalled and incase, cost is 
made absolute within the timeframe, the 
appellant is granted time upto 3rd August, 2012 
to remove the defects. Further, in case cost is 
paid and defects are removed, the appeal be 
listed for orders on 4th August, 2012. 
 (V.K. Bist, J.) 
 27.07.2012

IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
APPEAL FROM ORDER No. 294 of 2012 
State of Uttarakhand through Superintending Engineer 
ManeriBhali State-II Circle, Joshiyara, Uttarkashi. 
 ..…Appellant/Defendant. 
Versus 
M/s. Hydel Construction Pvt. Ltd. Dehradun 
 ….. Respondent. 
Hon’ble B.S. Verma, J.
(Delay Condonation application No.6388 of 2012) 
(Stay application No. of 2012) 
 Sri T.A. Khan, Dy. Advocate General assisted by 
Sri I.P. Kohli, Standing Counsel for the appellant/State. 
 Sri V.K. Kohli, Senior Advocate assisted by Sri 
H.M. Bhatia, Advocate for the respondent. 
 Heard learned counsel for the appellant on delay 
condonation application No.6388 of 2012 for condoning the 
delay in filing the appeal. 
 Perused the affidavit accompanying the 
application. Delay has sufficiently been explained in the 
affidavit. Therefore, delay condonation application is 
allowed. The delay is condoned. 
 Admit the appeal. 
 Summon the lower court record and record of 
arbitral proceedings also. 
 List this appeal after the lower court record is 
received. 
 Also heard on Stay application. 
 This appeal from order has been preferred by the 
appellant against the judgment and order dated 06.01.2012 
passed by the District Judge, Dehradun in Arbitration Case 
No.64 of 2007 State of Uttarakhand Vs. M/s. Hydel 
Construction Pvt. Ltd. Whereby the learned District Judge  2
has rejected the objection U/S 34 of Arbitration & 
Conciliation Act of the appellant against the arbitral award 
dated 08.04.2007 passed by the Arbitral Tribunal in respect 
of the claims regarding out of extra item of ues of steel fibre 
in shortcrete by the respondent herein arising from Principal 
agreement No.2/SE/1980-81 dated 30.03.1981 . 
 Learned Dy. Advocate General appearing on 
behalf of State/appellant has contended that respondent 
wrote a letter dated 25.11.2003 which is annexure No.6 to 
the appeal, to the petitioner-department wherein it is 
mentioned in the para 2 that “As regards our rates for supply 
and placing of the scanfibre with shortcrete, the same shall be 
as per the actual cost of the material at site 10% of the cost at 
site as labour and equipment charges and 20% overheads 
and profit on the same”. It is also requested that sanction 
may kindly be granted for the same. This letter was never 
cancelled nor withdrawn by the respondent. As above the 
rate of Rs.128.17 per Kg. was calculated by the respondent 
whereas the petitioner/department has rated the same at 
Rs.119. per Kg. This fact is not disputed that appellant￾department has accepted the supply and use of shortcrete 
as mentioned in the letter. 
 By the perusal of the objections, which have been 
filed as annexure No.7 to the appeal whereby it is clearly 
mentioned in the para No.5 that the work was treated as 
extra items. Ultimately the work continues and this work 
was decided to be “extra item” for which the rates were to be 
analysed. 
 A dispute arose between the parties regarding 
rates of extra item of “use of Scanfibre Steel in shortcrete” 
instead of the wire mesh which was being used earlier which 
was referred to the Hon’ble Arbitral Tribunal. 
 Learned Tribunal, after hearing the parties, 
considering the objections as well as the opinion of Expert 
Sri B.B.L. Mittal, Chief Engineer/Director, State Engineer’s  3
Academy, Uttaranchal and also perusal of the documents 
available on the record, came to the conclusion that 
respondent is entitle for the rate of Rs.220/- per kg. for 
scanfibre steel in short create for entire period. Of course, 
initially the work was assigned to the respondent on 
experimental basis at the rate of Rs. 95/- per kg. and final 
rate was to be negotiated between the parties. 
 Aggrieved by the said award passed by the 
learned Tribunal, State filed the objection before District 
Judge, Dehradun under Section 34 of the Arbitration & 
Conciliation Act, 1996 which was dismissed vide impugned 
order dated 06.01.2012 in Arbitration Case No.64 of 2007. 
Learned District Judge has also committed any manifest 
error of law in rejecting the objection of the appellant. 
 Since the award is a money decree. In view of the 
Order 41 Rule 1(3) of CPC makes provision that 
“where the appeal is against a decree for 
payment of money, the appellant shall, 
within such time as the Appellate Court 
may allow, deposit the amount disputed in 
the appeal or furnish such security in 
respect thereof as the Court may think fit”. 
 The Order 41 Rule 5 (3)(a) of CPC provides that 
substantial loss may result to the party applying for stay of 
execution unless the order is made. 
 In view of the above, as an interim measure, it is 
directed that the execution of the award shall remain stayed, 
if appellant deposits entire decree amount under award with 
the Registry of this Court within a period of two months from 
today. (Stay application stands disposed of). 
 
 (B.S. Verma, J.) 
 21.08.2012 JKJ

orders.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Miscellaneous Application No. 12796 of 2013
In 
Appeal from Order No. 294 of 2012
State of Uttarakhand. .……….. Appellant 
 
Versus 
M/s Hydel Construction Pvt. Ltd. ………… Respondent. 
Mr. T.A. Khan, Deputy Advocate General, with Mr. Pankaj Sharma, Brief Holder, for 
the State of Uttarakhand / appellant. 
Mr. V.K. Kohli, Senior Advocate, assisted by Mr. H.M. Bhatia, Advocate for the 
respondent. 
Hon’ble B.S. Verma, J.
 This Miscellaneous Application has been filed praying for release 
of the amount deposited by the appellant in compliance of the order dated 
21.08.2012 in favour of the respondent. 
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties. 
3. Brief facts of the case are that certain disputes arose between the 
appellant State of Uttarakhand and the respondent M/s Hydel 
Construction Pvt. Ltd., which were referred to the Arbitral Tribunal. The 
Arbitral Tribunal gave its award on 08.04.2007. The present appellant 
filed an Application under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation 
Act before the District Judge, Dehradun. After hearing the parties, the 
Application filed under Section 34 was dismissed by the learned District 
Judge, Dehradun, vide order dated 06.01.2012. Hence, the present appeal 
was filed on behalf of the State, which was admitted on 21.08.2012. This 
Court, at the time of admitting the appeal, directed the appellant State to 
deposit the entire amount directed to be paid vide the award passed by the 
Arbitral Tribunal, within a period of eight weeks.  2
4. The learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent 
contended that the project of Maneri Bhali Phase II, after its completion, 
has already started generation of electricity and the respondent is being 
deprived of its payment. 
5. Having considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the 
appellant and the learned counsel for the respondent, Miscellaneous 
Application Nos. 12796 of 2013 is disposed of with a direction that 25% 
of the amount deposited by the appellant shall be released in favour of the 
respondent without furnishing any security and 25% of the amount 
deposited by the appellant shall be released in favour of the respondent on 
furnishing a bank guarantee. Rest of the amount deposited by the 
appellant be deposited in a Fixed Deposit scheme to prevent loss of 
interest on the said sum. 
6. List this appeal for final hearing in the week commencing 24th
February, 2014. 
 (B.S. Verma, J.) 
 31.12.2013
